title: Regional handoff rehearsal and KV-cache sanity inspector
creator: Aisha Martinez
description:
Goal: Build a rehearsal harness and a lightweight ‘sanity inspector’ for regional handoffs that validates KV-cache health, prefix prefill integrity, and fallback-model compatibility before any production cutover. The inspector is a combined readiness check (k-v prefix coverage, prefetch worker health, model-variant compatibility) and a rehearsal runner that executes controlled canary handoffs without impacting live traffic.

Why: We see intermittent degradation after region cutover when cache warmth and model quantization mismatch combine with autoscaler ramp delays. This ticket reduces blast radius by fencing cutovers behind a reproducible readiness score and automated remediation suggestions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Implement KV-cache health probe emitting: kv_prefix_hit_ratio, kv_prefetch_fill_rate, kv_prefetch_inflight, prefetch_worker_queue_depth (metrics format: prometheus-friendly).
- Add a composite readiness_score (0-100) calculated from those signals plus model-variant compatibility checks and recent activation_latency_p99.
- Rehearsal harness that runs a staged handoff against a reserved canary shard (no customer traffic) and records: cache_fill_timeline, activation_errors, model_fallback_events.
- Gate: readiness_score >= 78 required to permit automated handoff; if score < 78 the system surfaces remediation playbook recommending: cap prefetch concurrency / increase prefill window / promote warm caches.
- Integration tests and a small-scale lab run that demonstrates successful handoff with quantized and non-quantized model variants.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change global routing policy definitions or the global election/quorum algorithm. It focuses on pre-cutover verification and rehearsal automation.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Instrument runtime to export the four KV metrics and activation_latency_p99 (ENG change).
2) Implement inspector service (stateless) that polls metrics and computes readiness_score; expose REST endpoint used by the orchestrator.
3) Rehearsal runner that can create a temporary canary shard, prefill prefixes using synthetic traces, and simulate a cutover (transfer routing weights).
4) Add remediation hints in Console UI and CLI output for SREs.
5) Run three consecutive dry-runs in staging across 2 regions; measure regressions and tune readiness threshold.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Prefill noise: synthetic prefill can create load spikes; limit concurrency and throttle to match typical per-region QPS.
- Storage IO saturation during large prefill; we will add a conservative concurrency cap and backoff.
- Readiness_score tuning may require several lab rehearsals — initial threshold conservative at 78.

Rollout plan:
- Feature-flag inspector behind staging-only flag for initial runs.
- Merge instrumentation + readiness endpoint (runtime + inspector).
- Execute 3 rehearsals in staging.
- Run a pilot on a low-traffic customer region with on-call coverage.
- Gradual enablement for automated cutover gating after 2 weeks of successful pilots.

Metrics to monitor post-rollout:
- Post-cutover error rate delta (should be <= 0.5% increase)
- Time-to-stable (time until latency returns to baseline after cutover)
- False-negative rate (failed rehearsal but successful manual cutover)
- Prefill IO throttling events

Notes: This ticket intentionally includes KV cache focus rather than full fleet priming; follow-up tickets will integrate quota-aware prefill and cross-region prefilling coordination.
